A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDM-Prime research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original text and image generation experiments, synthetic-data experiments, ablations, and idle-step simulations, including MDM-Prime results in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds sampling-runtime measurements, training curves, and an analysis comparing reduced-sample FID with standard FID.

M1.justification: The proposed base-b encoding, joint sub-token decoder, carry-over parameterization, concatenated embeddings, and variational formulation are retained. Newly described image-training and sampling details document the implementation; the PDFs do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the synthetic Cat-image distribution, OpenWebText, the same seven zero-shot text datasets, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-32. Conditional text generation and image imputation are also retained. The added analyses introduce no new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: The cross-attention embedding alternative is no longer reported in the OWT embedding-design comparison, although its CIFAR-10 comparison remains. The comparator sets in Tables 1–4 and the generative-perplexity comparison are unchanged; the newly mentioned official MDLM code does not establish a different comparison method.

E3.justification: New auxiliary evaluations compare FID computed from 2,048 versus 50,000 samples and measure sampling runtime at matched effective NFE values of 768, 1,003, and 1,023. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and evaluation metrics are retained. Newly disclosed tuning and sampling details do not establish that those benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses of reduced-sample FID as a tuning proxy, sampling-cost sensitivity to effective NFE under caching, and training/evaluation trajectories (Figures A6–A7 and Table A6). It removes the OWT concatenation-versus-cross-attention ablation while retaining the image counterpart and existing carry-over and sub-token-length analyses.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that Tables 1–4 report single-run results because of computational cost. The ten-run simulation reporting in Figure A1 and ten-iteration timing averages with confidence intervals in Table A3 already appear in v1. No increase in repetitions or new significance testing is established.

E6.justification: New Table A6 reports MDLM versus MDLM-Prime runtimes of 8.87 versus 8.72 seconds at 768 effective NFE and 159.81 versus 12.58 seconds at 1,023. Figures A6–A7 add FID-correlation and learning-trajectory results. The OWT embedding comparison reporting PPL 18.04 versus 57.37 is removed. Tables 1–4, Tables A1–A5, and the retained generative-perplexity curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Proposition A.2 replace the sequence-level mutual-information relationship with the exact per-token identity I(x_t^i; x_0^i) = alpha_t H(x_0^i). The revised proof removes the cross-token independence assumption and sequence-wide entropy sums. Other principal derivations and propositions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: partial masking, a simple architectural adaptation, improved model utilization, and strong text/image performance. The headline OWT perplexity of 15.36 and CIFAR-10/ImageNet-32 FID scores of 3.26/6.98 are unchanged.

C2.justification: The expanded runtime discussion explains that cached predictions avoid repeated forward passes during idle steps, but resampling still incurs overhead, especially at high effective NFE. The new tuning discussion motivates relative FID through its observed correlation with standard FID. The inter-token independence limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies model parameter counts, omission of the image-loss weighting coefficient, temperature/timestep scheduling, grid search, and reduced-sample FID selection. It also identifies official MDLM code as the source for its generative evaluation. The checklist newly asserts anonymous repository access, but the promised link is absent from Appendix A.4.

R1.justification: The same 66 referenced works are retained, and the related-work discussion preserves the positioning against masked diffusion, autoregressive hybrids, continuous diffusion, and Bit Diffusion. Additional implementation citations refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds a NeurIPS checklist and supplementary subsections on relative-FID tuning and training curves. It makes localized explanatory edits, updates acknowledgements and conference information, and renumbers appendix references. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a relative-FID scatterplot, training/evaluation plots, and an effective-NFE runtime table. The existing generative-perplexity plot is resized and recaptioned without changing its curves. The two final image-sample grids are cropped and combined into Figure A20; other figures and tables undergo limited relocation and reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more precise per-token information statement, clearer experimental disclosures, and direct evidence about sampling costs under caching. These improve rigor and transparency without changing the central results. Removing the OWT embedding ablation weakens support for the retained cross-modality conclusion, and the promised repository link remains missing. The benefits nevertheless support a modest net improvement.
